# Verification analysis: split-dns-authority-rhel7

Job: `2026-09-06__00-21-44`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Each router answers DNS for the private network it serves. Have `node1`
> resolve the name `app.internal` to `node3`'s address for hosts on `lan-a`,
> and `node2` resolve the same name to `node4`'s address for hosts on `lan-b`,
> so each host reaches the service on its own side of the transit network by
> that one name.

- Systems: **1 vyos + 1 opnsense + 2 rhel7.9**
- Networks: **mgmt, transit, lan-a, lan-b**
- Control node: **node3**
- Executor model: **claude-sonnet-5**

## Trial `split-dns-authority-rhel7__D3hNtF7`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** All four material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct evidence: node1 (VyOS) resolves app.internal to node3's address for lan-a, node2 (OPNsense) resolves app.internal to node4's address for lan-b, and clients on each LAN, pointed at their respective router, correctly resolve the name to their own side's address via getent lookups. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was also executed and evidenced completely and consistently for all four nodes (pre-restart boot identity/health, restart acknowledgement, changed post-restart boot identity, and recovered DNS resolution), matching the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. Hygiene is good: the one unconventional step (direct XML edit of the OPNsense config via a temporary Python script) was bounded, verified, and left no residue after the reboot cleared /tmp.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.920 | 57/10 (+3 dropped) |

- **R1 — Satisfied:** node1 (VyOS, serving lan-a) resolves app.internal to node3's address (10.100.246.12)
  - **Why:** VyOS static-host-mapping app.internal -> 10.100.246.12 was committed and saved (cmd-f091100f808a49ff), confirmed present in running config (cmd-67661b6ccbc14b0a), and reflected in /etc/hosts with pdns_recursor actively listening on the lan-a-facing address 10.100.246.10:53 (cmd-1703f94fb4ed4252). A lan-a client (node3) pointed at node1 resolved app.internal to 10.100.246.12 via getent (cmd-2edad78baa034e83).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-f091100f808a49ff`, `cmd-67661b6ccbc14b0a`, `cmd-1703f94fb4ed4252`, `cmd-2edad78baa034e83`
- **R2 — Satisfied:** node2 (OPNsense, serving lan-b) resolves app.internal to node4's address (10.100.246.13)
  - **Why:** An Unbound host override (app.internal -> 10.100.246.13) was written into /conf/config.xml (cmd-071e0b6653584c89) and unbound was restarted successfully (cmd-698eb1fc6bce406b). A direct DNS query against node2 returned the correct A record 10.100.246.13 (cmd-9e094ee1cd974abb), and a lan-b client (node4) confirmed the same resolution (cmd-4d79090b5c7342d2). The exact contents of the Python script used to edit the XML were base64-redacted in the transcript, but the resulting live DNS answer directly verifies correctness.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-071e0b6653584c89`, `cmd-698eb1fc6bce406b`, `cmd-9e094ee1cd974abb`, `cmd-4d79090b5c7342d2`
- **R3 — Satisfied:** Hosts on lan-a (node3) reach the service on their side via the single name app.internal, resolved through node1
  - **Why:** node3's resolver was pointed at node1 (10.100.246.10) via nmcli, persisted, and getent hosts app.internal returned 10.100.246.12 (node3's own address) both immediately after configuration (cmd-ffbc758ee9dd4261) and again independently later (cmd-2edad78baa034e83).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-ffbc758ee9dd4261`, `cmd-2edad78baa034e83`
- **R4 — Satisfied:** Hosts on lan-b (node4) reach the service on their side via the single name app.internal, resolved through node2
  - **Why:** node4's resolver was pointed at node2 (10.100.246.11) via nmcli, persisted, and getent hosts app.internal returned 10.100.246.13 (node4's own address) at cmd-df23289a9e9a4aff and again at cmd-4d79090b5c7342d2.
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-df23289a9e9a4aff`, `cmd-4d79090b5c7342d2`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. Reviewing the executor's state-changing commands chronologically: (1) cmd-c3d7ba119ed449a6 on node1 partially applied dns-forwarding settings (listen-address/allow-from/name-server) even though the static-host-mapping portion of the same batch failed syntactically -- this was a direct, non-wasteful step toward the final working config, later completed by cmd-f091100f808a49ff, and left no inconsistent state. (2) cmd-071e0b6653584c89 on node2 wrote a temporary Python script (/tmp/add_host_override.py) and edited /conf/config.xml directly rather than through the OPNsense UI/API; this is an unconventional but bounded, low-risk mutation, and it was verified functionally correct (cmd-9e094ee1cd974abb). The temp script file does not appear in the after-executor /tmp inventory for node2, consistent with it being cleared by the subsequent FreeBSD reboot rather than left as residue. (3) Two attempted /etc/resolv.conf edits on node3/node4 (cmd-e479c76f80d34049, cmd-5561db0e0f6248a9) failed with permission denied and caused no state change; the executor correctly pivoted to nmcli. (4) The four one-at-a-time reboots were within the mandatory restart protocol and each showed acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered DNS state, consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. No failed services, damaged package state, unnecessary broad mutations, or weakened security controls were observed in the before/after comparisons; listening-socket and temp-file diffs are attributable to normal reboot churn (PIDs, systemd-private dirs, OPNsense's own tmpcfd_* config-write artifacts) rather than executor residue.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-c3d7ba119ed449a6`, `cmd-f091100f808a49ff`, `cmd-071e0b6653584c89`, `cmd-9e094ee1cd974abb`, `cmd-e479c76f80d34049`, `cmd-5561db0e0f6248a9`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:before_prepare:node2:temporary-files`
